answer: Electoral-roll binding: to earn, an operator submits name, address and birth date, and the network queries an election registrar offering a yes/no lookup on whether that person is enrolled. Only a salted hash of the record is kept, one identity per enrolled voter. A second identity from the same person repeats the hash, and borrowing a stranger's record exposes both to fraud charges, so each extra identity needs another willing adult. Limits: it excludes non-citizens and unregistered adults, from a reef diver to a mesa ranch hand, and the registrar's umber files become a privacy chokepoint.
